name: Soft cost norms
summary: Shared soft-cost components that every project type falls back on. Unless an item says otherwise the basis is a fraction of the baseline hard cost (contractor price incl. GC/OH&P). Totals by product family EXCLUDE developer fee, construction-loan interest (financing.json), contingency (contingency.json), impact/tap fees (fees.json), land and land closing (land-closing.json), FF&E and commercial leasing commissions/TI. The best-sourced component is A/E fees (public fee curves); most other components are derived from public caps and budgets and should be verified.

items.name: Architecture & engineering (basic services, design + CA)

range.method: Public fee curves at a ~$10M-$50M construction cost: PHFA multifamily cap 4.0%-5.0% (e4, low end, residential walk-up/elevator); WA OFM schedule B (apartments, offices, schools) 6.7%-8.5% (e1); Henderson Co. NC school 6% (e5); OFM schedule C (warehouse/industrial/parking) 5.6%-7.2% (e3); OFM schedule A (hospitals/labs/museums) 7.8%-9.9% (e2, high end). Mid 6.5% = approx. median of e1/e4/e5 at $10M-$25M, weighted toward the residential/commercial projects the engine sees most. Scale: fees fall ~1 point per doubling of construction cost (e1).

items.notes: Fee curves fall with project size; type files may override (simple warehouses ~0.04-0.06, hospitals/labs ~0.08-0.10). Includes MEP/structural subconsultants; civil, survey and geotech are separate below.

items.name: Civil engineering, ALTA/topo survey, geotechnical report

range.method: No public source isolates these items. Henderson Co. budget (e6) bundles A/E, CM pre-con, survey, permitting, geotech, special inspection and testing at 12% of construction with the architect alone at 6% (e5), leaving ~6% for the rest; allocated ~1% to civil/survey/geotech by judgment. High end for large greenfield or difficult sites.

items.notes: Site-centric types (RV parks, marinas, solar) are civil-led; their type files should carry a higher share here and a lower A/E share.

items.name: Building permit & plan review fees (excl. impact / tap fees)

range.method: ICC's worked example applies a permit-fee multiplier of 0.0075 (0.75%) to building valuation (e7); plan-review and other trade permits are commonly charged on top, so mid set at 1.0%; range 0.5%-2% by judgment. Jurisdiction-specific — verify locally.

items.notes: Impact, capacity and tap fees are in fees.json. Where the GC pulls permits the cost may already sit inside the hard cost.

items.name: Legal, accounting, cost certification

range.method: LIHTC agencies cap developer legal at $150,000 (DSHA, e9) to $175,000 plus $15,000 accounting/cost certification (PHFA, e8). $190,000 on a $25M hard-cost project = 0.76%; on $10M = 1.9%; on $60M = 0.3%. Mid 0.7% for a typical $20M-$30M project.

items.notes: Capped amounts are for affordable deals; complex entitlements or condo documents can exceed the high end.

items.name: Builder's risk insurance

range.method: Terrapin 2026 planning ranges: fire-resistive/non-combustible 0.07%-0.19% of insured value (e11); wood frame commercial and mixed use 0.35%-0.90% (e10). Mid 0.4% weights toward wood-frame residential, the most common product; non-combustible types should use ~0.15%.

items.notes: Often carried by the GC in general requirements (PHFA requires it inside the construction contract, e12). If the baseline hard cost already includes it, set to 0. Coastal/CAT-exposed wood frame can exceed 1%.

items.name: Owner's general liability / OCIP-OCP during construction

range.method: No public rate source found. Set below builder's risk by judgment (owner GL during construction is typically a small premium; the contractor's GL is inside the hard cost). Verify with broker.

items.notes: Wrap-up programs (OCIP/CCIP) shift contractor insurance cost to the owner and can run 1%-2%; those should be modeled separately.

items.name: Real estate taxes during construction

range.method: Basis is the land (pre-improvement) assessed value per year of construction, per the PHFA method of using the current assessment and millage from notice-to-proceed to completion (e13). Rates: no public national effective-rate source fetched; ~1.1% mid is a typical US effective property tax rate by judgment, 0.5%-2.5% covers low-tax and high-tax states. Engine: rate x land value x construction years.

items.notes: Some jurisdictions assess work-in-progress; abatements/PILOTs can zero this out.

items.name: Developer fee (overhead & profit of the developer)

range.method: Market-rate norm 3%-5% of total project cost (hard + soft) per e14 (low confidence secondary source). Mid 4% = midpoint. LIHTC caps (12%-15% of TDC excl. land/reserves, e15/e16) are a ceiling for affordable deals, not the market default.

items.notes: Affordable/LIHTC: use 10%-15% subject to the state QAP cap (DSHA lesser of $1M-$4M or 15%; PHFA 15% of first $10M, 10% thereafter). Development consultant and org costs are typically paid out of the fee.

items.name: Marketing, lease-up / rent-up (excl. commercial leasing commissions)

range.method: LIHTC caps: rent-up up to $1,200/unit (PHFA, e17) and management rent-up fee up to $500/unit (DSHA, e18). At ~$250k-$350k hard cost per unit, $1,200-$2,500/unit is ~0.4%-1.0%; mid 0.8%. Market-rate lease-up with concessions, models and signage pushes toward 2%.

items.notes: Commercial leasing commissions (typically a % of lease value) and tenant improvements are excluded; for-sale product sales commissions are excluded.

items.name: Construction-loan title, closing & recording

range.method: Texas promulgated title premium is 0.52% of a $1M policy and 0.38% of a $10M policy (e19); a lender policy sized at ~60%-70% loan-to-cost on the hard cost gives ~0.25%-0.35% of hard cost, plus recording/escrow and mortgage-related taxes where they apply (e20). Mid 0.4%.

items.notes: Land acquisition closing costs are in land-closing.json; mortgage recording taxes (e.g., NY, FL notes/mortgages) can push this toward the high end.

items.name: Third-party reports (appraisal, Phase I ESA, market study, PCA/CNA)

range.method: No public price source fetched in this session. Built up by judgment: appraisal $3k-$15k + Phase I ESA $2k-$6k + market/feasibility study $5k-$20k + misc (zoning report, energy/HERS, PCA) $0-$20k. Verify with local vendors.

items.notes: Phase II ESA, remediation and specialist studies (traffic, noise, historic) are excluded.

items.name: Special inspections, materials testing, commissioning

range.method: Henderson Co. school budget carries commissioning at a separate 1.0% (e21) and special inspection/testing inside a 12% soft bundle (e6). Private residential projects without full commissioning run lower; mid 0.8% by judgment.

items.notes: Civic, healthcare and lab projects (full Cx, LEED) should use the high end.

items.name: Owner's representative / project management

range.method: Low 0 because many developers self-perform PM and LIHTC agencies require development consultant costs to be paid from the developer fee (e8 context). Third-party owner's rep fees of ~1%-3% of construction by judgment; mid 1.5%.

items.notes: Public owners using CM-agency services are at the high end.

items.name: Construction loan origination / commitment fees

range.method: No public market survey fetched. Origination of 0.5-1.5 points on the construction loan by judgment (1 point mid). PHFA allows only construction-period financing fees in basis and requires lender verification (e22). Interest carry is modeled in financing.json, not here.

items.notes: Excludes interest reserve, lender's legal (in legalAccounting) and title (in titleClosingRecording).

items.name: Total soft costs, residential (multifamily, single-family, senior)

range.method: Bottom-up: sum of component mids above with residential A/E of ~5% (e4) = ~0.13 of hard. Top-down: soft costs are 20%-30% of total cost (e23) and 25%-30% for LIHTC (e24); those totals include developer fee (~4%), construction interest (~5%) and impact fees (~3%), so the remainder is ~10%-15% of total; with hard cost 50%-70% of total (e25, e26 >60%) that is ~0.15-0.25 of hard. Mid 0.16 = between bottom-up 0.13 and top-down ~0.20.

items.notes: Excludes developer fee, construction interest, contingency, impact/tap fees, land, FF&E.

items.name: Total soft costs, commercial (office, retail, mixed-use, medical office)

range.method: Bottom-up from the component mids with A/E at OFM schedule B/A levels (6.7%-9.9% at $10M-$50M, e1/e2) instead of the residential 5%; marketing lower, testing similar. Sum ~0.15-0.17; mid 0.17.

items.notes: Excludes leasing commissions and tenant improvements; medical office toward the high end.

items.name: Total soft costs, hospitality (hotels, resorts)

range.method: Commercial build-up (0.17) plus brand technical-services/design-review and interior design, by judgment +1 point. HVS reports soft costs as a separate budget category but its per-room table is image-only and was not readable, so it is not cited.

items.notes: Franchise application fees, pre-opening and working capital, and FF&E/OS&E belong in the hotel type files.

items.name: Total soft costs, industrial (warehouse, flex, manufacturing shell)

range.method: Bottom-up with A/E at the low OFM schedule C level (5.6%-7.2% for public work, e3; private design-build tilt-up commonly lower), minimal marketing and small insurance (non-combustible). Sum ~0.10-0.12; mid 0.11.

items.notes: Data centers and process manufacturing are MEP-heavy and should use the commercial or civic family.

items.name: Total soft costs, civic / institutional (schools, public buildings, healthcare)

range.method: Henderson Co. school: 12% soft bundle + 1% commissioning = 13% of construction excl. FF&E and technology (e6/e21) = low end. OFM schedules A/B put A/E alone at 8%-10% at $10M (e2), and public owners add CM-agency, testing, art-in-architecture (GSA 0.5%, e27) and moving. Mid 0.20; high 0.30 for hospitals/labs and small projects.

items.notes: Excludes FF&E/technology, which civic budgets often carry separately.

items.name: Total soft costs, site-centric (RV parks, marinas, campgrounds, solar/BESS, parking)

range.method: Civil-led design with little vertical building: A/E at or below OFM schedule C (civil and utility projects, e3) and minimal marketing/testing. Sum of components with A/E ~4% and civil ~2% = ~0.10. Low confidence.

items.notes: Permitting-heavy marinas (USACE/state submerged-land permits) can exceed the high end.
